title: Awareness Campaign: What It Is and How to Run One on Meta, Google and TikTok
summary: An awareness campaign gets your brand in front of many new people before they buy. Goals, metrics and a seven-step plan for Meta, Google and TikTok.
body_markdown:
## The short answer


- An **awareness campaign** is paid advertising built to put your brand in front of many new people who do not know you yet, measured by reach, impressions, frequency and recall instead of sales.
- Each platform has a home for it: the Awareness objective on Meta, Reach and video view objectives on TikTok, and brand awareness and reach goals on Google Display, Video and Demand Gen.
- Judge it on cost per thousand impressions (CPM), reach, frequency and lift. Clicks and purchases come later in the funnel.
- Run it in seven steps: one goal, broad audience, the right objective, short hooked creative, a frequency plan, the right metrics, then lift and follow-up.


## What an awareness campaign is


An awareness campaign is the top of the funnel. Its job is to make a large number of the right people familiar with your brand, product or message before they are ready to buy. It does not ask for the sale. It asks for recognition.


That changes how you set it up. The audience is wide, the creative is memorable rather than persuasive, and success is measured in how many people saw the ad and remembered it. Conversion campaigns for the same brand then pick up people who already know you, which is why awareness spend often makes later campaigns cheaper per acquisition.


Awareness sits at the first stage of the models described in[awareness stages](https://www.sprites.ai/awareness-stages) , and it is one of the main uses of the formats in[types of advertising](https://www.sprites.ai/blog/types-of-advertising) . The persuasion methods you choose come from[advertising techniques](https://www.sprites.ai/blog/advertising-techniques) .


## Goals and metrics that fit awareness


Pick one primary goal. Mixing them muddies the read.


Goal What it counts Best metric Watch out for


Reach Unique people who saw the ad Cost per 1,000 people reached Frequency can be too low to build memory


Impressions Total times the ad was shown CPM A small group can see it many times


Recall People who remember the ad Estimated ad recall lift Needs enough budget for the platform to measure it


Video views Views of a set length Cost per view, view rate A view is not the same as attention


Brand search People who search for you afterwards Branded search volume Slow and affected by other channels


The other numbers to track are frequency (average times one person saw the ad) and CPM. Use the[CPM calculator](https://www.sprites.ai/tools/cpm-calculator) to turn spend and impressions into the figure you compare across platforms. If your awareness ads are video, track the opening seconds with[hook rate](https://www.sprites.ai/blog/hook-rate) .


## How the platforms handle awareness


All three platforms name this goal differently and optimize for different things. The choice of objective tells the platform which people to show the ad to, so it matters.


Platform Where you set it What it optimizes for


Meta (Facebook and Instagram) Awareness objective in Ads Manager Reach, impressions, ad recall lift or ThruPlay depending on the optimization you pick


TikTok Awareness objectives in TikTok Ads Manager, such as Reach and video views Showing to as many people as possible, or to people likely to watch the video


Google Display, Video or Demand Gen campaigns with a brand awareness and reach goal Reach and impressions across YouTube, Display and Discover surfaces


Names and menus on each platform change from time to time, so check the current option in the ad account before you build. Creative specs live on the[Meta specs](https://www.sprites.ai/ad-specs/meta) and[TikTok specs](https://www.sprites.ai/ad-specs/tiktok) pages, and[Facebook ad sizes](https://www.sprites.ai/blog/facebook-ad-sizes) covers the placements.


## How to run an awareness campaign, step by step


1. **Set one awareness goal.** Pick reach (how many different people), impressions (how many times ads show) or recall (how many remember you). Choose one. Reach and recall pull the platform in different directions.
2. **Define the audience broadly.** Use location, age range and a few interest or intent signals. Awareness works by reaching many people who could buy, not a tight retargeting list.
3. **Pick the platform objective.** On Meta choose the Awareness objective. On TikTok choose a Reach or video views objective. On Google run a Display, Video or Demand Gen campaign set to brand awareness and reach.
4. **Build short creative with a clear hook.** Lead with the brand and the idea in the first three seconds. Make three to five variations so the platform has something to compare.
5. **Set a frequency and budget plan.** Decide how many times one person should see the ad per week. Divide the budget over the flight so spend stays steady.
6. **Launch and read the right metrics.** Watch reach, frequency, CPM and video view rates. Do not judge awareness by clicks or purchases.
7. **Measure lift and follow up.** Run a brand lift or recall check where the platform offers one, then retarget the people who engaged with a conversion campaign.


Most failures come from steps 1 and 6. Teams pick reach, then judge the campaign on clicks, and cancel a working campaign.


## A worked example: a local meal-kit brand


This is an illustration with made-up numbers, not a benchmark. A meal-kit company launches in a new city with a $6,000 awareness budget over four weeks.


Item Plan


Goal Reach: 300,000 different people in the city


Audience Adults 25 to 54 within the city, no interest narrowing


Creative Three 15 second videos, each opening with the brand name and a dish on the table


Frequency target About 3 views per person over the four weeks


Budget pacing $1,500 a week, steady


Read-out Reach, frequency, CPM and a recall survey at the end


Follow-up A conversion campaign to people who watched most of a video


Notice what is missing. There is no landing page goal, no sales target, and no click-through requirement. The campaign is judged on whether 300,000 people in the target city saw the brand three times.


## Mistakes that waste awareness budget


- **Judging by clicks.** Reach campaigns are not built to produce clicks.
- **Too narrow an audience.** A tight audience pushes frequency up and reach down.
- **One creative.** Fatigue sets in. See[animated ads](https://www.sprites.ai/blog/animated-ads) for a cheap way to build variations from the same script.
- **No follow-up.** Awareness without a retargeting layer leaves value on the table.
- **Stopping early.** Recall builds over weeks. Cutting after three days measures nothing.

## Frequently asked questions


### What is an awareness campaign?


An awareness campaign is paid advertising designed to make many new people familiar with your brand before they are ready to buy. It is measured on reach, impressions, frequency and recall rather than clicks or sales.


### What is the goal of an awareness campaign?


The goal is recognition. You want the right people to see your brand enough times that they remember it, so later campaigns, search and word of mouth convert them more easily.


### What metrics should I use for an awareness campaign?


Use reach, impressions, frequency, CPM and, where the platform offers it, an ad recall or brand lift result. For video, add view rate and hook rate. Avoid judging it on clicks or purchases.


### How do I run an awareness campaign on Meta?


Create a campaign with the Awareness objective, choose a broad audience, pick an optimization such as reach or ad recall lift, and upload short creative. Set a steady budget and watch reach and frequency, not clicks.


### How long should an awareness campaign run?


Run it long enough for recall to build, which is usually several weeks, not days. Stopping early means you measure the learning phase instead of the campaign.


### What is the difference between awareness and conversion campaigns?


An awareness campaign aims for reach and memory with a broad audience. A conversion campaign aims for sales or sign-ups from people closer to buying. Awareness fills the funnel, conversion campaigns close it.
